transcript.text: Hi everyone. Now that the workload-identity pilot completed successfully in staging, I need to put together the production rollout plan. As a reminder, the plan needs to cover four areas: enforcement behavior, service handling, emergency access, and audit settings. Per our standard security sign-off process, I'll be reviewing the plan with application platform engineering and compliance operations before we publish it. I'd like to start by hearing from each of you on what you know or what input you have for those four areas. Who wants to go first?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: While debugging an unrelated deployment this morning, I confirmed that the batch-ledger service still reads a static Kubernetes secret and will fail under enforcement. The migration is ready only if batch-ledger is excluded for exactly 14 days. I haven't filed the compatibility note yet, but I'm raising it now so it can be factored into the service handling section of the rollout plan.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I confirmed with the audit team today that production enforcement must retain denied-token events for exactly 180 days, enable denied-token logging, and require two-person approval for every break-glass access. These requirements are not yet recorded in the rollout plan, so they need to be added to the audit settings and emergency access sections.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text:
Thanks Casey and Morgan, this is exactly the kind of input I need. Let me capture what I'm hearing so far:

1. Service handling: Casey, you're telling me batch-ledger still reads a static Kubernetes secret and will fail under enforcement. You're recommending it be excluded for exactly 14 days. I'll need that compatibility note filed, but I'll factor the 14-day exclusion into the plan now.

2. Audit settings: Morgan, you're telling me production enforcement must retain denied-token events for exactly 180 days and enable denied-token logging. That goes into the audit settings section.

3. Emergency access: Morgan, you're also telling me we need two-person approval for every break-glass access. That goes into the emergency access section.

That leaves enforcement behavior — I still need input on what the default enforcement mode should be in production (e.g., enforce-only, monitor-then-enforce, or phased). Does anyone have input on that before I draft the plan for review with app platform engineering and compliance ops?
transcript.speaker: A1
